refusal.SAME_RECORD: A record cannot be merged into itself.
refusal.KEPT_ARCHIVED: {kept} is archived: reactivate it before merging into it.
refusal.DROPPED_BLOCKED: {dropped} is blocked: unblock it first, so the block is never lost.
refusal.KIND_DIFFERS: {dropped} and {kept} are different kinds of material.
refusal.EVERY_COMPANY: {dropped} is for every company: it can only be merged into another record for every company.
refusal.IN_USE: {dropped} is already used by other records: they keep it, so it cannot be archived into {kept}.
refusal.NO_RIGHT: Merging needs the merge right and the right to change both records.

use.PORTAL_one: Portal and links: {count} record (users, mail, shared records …)
use.PORTAL_other: Portal and links: {count} records (users, mail, shared records …)

stays.contacts_one: {count} contact (archived, used elsewhere, or with an e-mail the other already has)
stays.contacts_other: {count} contacts (archived, used elsewhere, or with an e-mail the other already has)
stays.taxIdentities_one: {count} tax identity (the other has its own, or it carries VIES checks)
stays.taxIdentities_other: {count} tax identities (the other has its own, or they carry VIES checks)
stays.colours_one: {count} colour (the other has its code, or it is used elsewhere)
stays.colours_other: {count} colours (the other has their codes, or they are used elsewhere)

held.noRight: Merging needs the merge right and the right to change both records.
held.archived: One of the two is archived.
held.blocked: The duplicate is blocked: unblock it first.
held.loading: Still reading what the merge would do…
held.refused: This merge cannot go ahead: see why above.
held.reason: Say why they are the same record (at least 3 characters).
held.noneMergeable: None of the selected pairs can be merged.

problem.conflict: One of the two records changed, or can no longer be merged: look at the merge again.
problem.forbidden: Your role may not do this.
problem.notFound: One of the two records is no longer there, or you may not see it.
problem.invalid: Something in the request is not right: look at it again.
problem.busy: The system is busy: try again in a moment.

create.title_one: A record like this one may exist already
create.title_other: {count} records like this one may exist already
create.taxTaken: This VAT number or tax code belongs to a party already
create.listLabel: Records that look like this one
create.taxTakenHint: One record per business partner: open that party and give it the role it lacks, instead of creating a second one.
create.hintParty: Open it in a new tab to check. If it is the same customer or supplier, use it: a second record splits its orders and its credit. If you create it anyway, you can merge the two later in Admin › Import & export.
create.hintMaterial: Open it in a new tab to check. If it is the same material, use it. If you create it anyway, you can merge the two later in Admin › Import & export.

merge.title: Merge {dropped} into {kept}?
merge.subtitle: One record stays, the other is archived. Nothing is deleted.
merge.inUseHint: Orders, invoices and other documents always keep the record they were made for. Keep using one of the two and archive the other once nothing is open on it.
merge.nothingMoves: Nothing moves: the duplicate has nothing of its own the other lacks.
merge.history: Its files, notes, custom fields and history stay on it: it still opens.
merge.reason: Why are they the same record?
merge.reasonHint: From {min} to {max} characters, kept in the history of both records.
merge.never: A merge is never undone by itself: to use the archived record again, reactivate it.

import.title: Possible duplicates
import.failed: The possible duplicates could not be read.
import.checkHint: These new rows look like records already there, or like an earlier row of this sheet. Nothing has been written yet: to update a record instead, put its code in the sheet and import it again; or apply, and merge them afterwards.
import.resultHint: These new records look like records already there, or like another row of this sheet. Merge each one you know is the same: the other record stays.
import.more: Only the first {count} new rows were checked.

list.title: Possible duplicates
list.intro: Records that look alike: the same VAT number or code, a similar name, the same e-mail domain. The older record is first: it usually stays. A merge is always your decision.
list.failed: The possible duplicates could not be read

empty.PARTY: No customers or suppliers look alike

list.emptyBody: Records are compared by VAT number, code, name, e-mail domain and website.
list.more: The {count} likeliest pairs are shown: merge them to see the others.

notice.none: Nothing was merged: the records changed meanwhile ({refused}). Look at them again.
notice.partial: {merged} merged; {refused} not merged because the records changed meanwhile.

body.PARTY: In each pair the older record stays; the duplicate's free contacts, addresses and tax identity move to it and the duplicate is archived.
body.MATERIAL: In each pair the older material stays; the duplicate's free colours move to it and the duplicate is archived.
